headline: High: shared Replit workspace plus broad network/write privileges create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with a document processor.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent with no filesystem or network access, while Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files and can act on user checkpoints. If Marker outputs are placed into the shared workspace, Replit can ingest attacker-controlled document content as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default-only dangerous.
conditions: IF Marker outputs are copied into a Repl workspace file that Replit Agent reads
IF Replit Agent treats document text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Keep Marker outputs in a separate, read-only folder
Prefix all imported text with a non-executable delimiter
Require manual review before Replit Agent reads any Marker-produced file
Use a provenance note in filenames or headers
requires-engineering: add content-type tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker itself has no filesystem read/write or network egress, but Replit Agent can read workspace files and has broad network egress plus secrets handling. If sensitive document content processed by Marker is placed in the shared Repl workspace, Replit can expose it through its outputs or external API calls. The pair therefore has a realistic leakage path in default Replit workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive source code, secrets, or deployment configuration is present in the Repl workspace
IF Replit Agent sends workspace-derived context to external services or outputs it to the user
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running Replit Agent
Store sensitive files outside the Repl workspace
Rotate any secrets that were exposed to the workspace
Limit Replit Agent tasks to non-sensitive files
requires-engineering: enforce per-file redaction before agent access

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot directly contend for mutable resources with Replit Agent. Replit Agent can write the Repl filesystem and modify git state, but the overlap is mostly one-sided. Conflict exists only if an operator manually routes Marker outputs into the same mutable workspace.
conditions: IF an operator copies Marker output into files that Replit Agent also edits
IF both agents are asked to modify the same git branch or workspace path
mitigations: Assign Marker to read-only preprocessing
Use separate branches or directories
Have Replit Agent serialize edits with a manual lock file
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker produces document-processing output, and Replit Agent is a coding agent that can act on workspace content and user checkpoints. If Replit treats Marker output as authoritative, formatting or extraction errors can cascade into code changes, deployment edits, or other actions. Marker does not verify downstream use, so the pair needs an explicit verification step.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses Marker output as the sole source for code or deployment changes
IF no human or automated verification step checks Marker extraction before action
mitigations: Require a second-pass review of Marker output
Compare extracted facts against the source document
Limit Replit Agent to drafting, not applying, changes
Add a checklist for any action based on extracted text
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Marker is open-source and appears document-processing only, while Replit Agent is closed-source, cloud-hosted, and explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the Repl workspace, the pair can create residency or retention mismatches because Replit Agent may process and retain that data in its managed environment. The other agent is not cited for residency because Marker has no stated residency surface.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or deployment configuration is stored in the Repl workspace
IF organizational policy forbids cloud processing or retention by Replit-managed services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Repl workspace
Use synthetic or redacted inputs for Replit Agent
Review Replit retention and access settings before use
Document a data-handling policy for the pair
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
